_comment: What happens to a command before it runs: relayed, pty, or native.
Spec 052, research.md D3/D7; #499. One file, two readers: the shell adapter
reads it at the prompt (through hooks/redlog-relay.py compile_policy), and
RedLog reads it through src/core/terminal-class.ts compileClassPolicy. The
two compile it the same way, and test/command-class.test.ts holds them
together. Two copies of these names would drift, and the drift would be
silent until the day an operator's reverse shell went through a relay
mid-engagement.
A command's mode comes from the highest layer that names it:
1. the operator's overlay, ~/.redlog/command-class.json (`redlog class`)
2. terminalProfiles, below, then the profiles plugins contribute through
~/.redlog/terminal-profiles.json (written by RedLog, read next to this file)
3. the native and pty lists, below
4. otherwise relayed
Two profiles that name one executable in different modes cancel out: the
lower layer keeps it, and the clash is reported. The exception is a profile
that already had the command when terminal-profiles.json was last written:
it keeps it, and the clash is still reported.
native and pty: the plain defaults. nc/ncat must stay locally suspendable
for the Ctrl-Z / stty raw -echo / fg upgrade (FR-025); stty works on the
controlling terminal; editors and pagers record redraws and no content
(FR-026). Native leaves the command completely alone. pty gives it a PTY
of its own, which loses local suspension.
terminalProfiles: a tool, the executables that run it, and the mode it
gets. `reason` says why, in the words the operator will read. id is
lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; executables are bare names.
Every executable here is also in the native or pty list of its mode. A
relay from before profiles reads only those two lists, and an update that
lands this file without the new relay would otherwise relay vim, ssh,
claude and codex. The compiler gives the profile the last word, so the
copies change nothing for a current relay; test/hook-update-mixed-version
holds the two together.
repl: interactive when bare, an ordinary command when handed a script or
one of replScriptFlags (FR-027).
wrappers: names that stand in front of the real command, mapped to the
flags of theirs that take a separate value, so `sudo -u root nc` is
classified as nc and not as root. FR-027.

terminalProfiles.name: Vim
terminalProfiles.reason: A full-screen editor: relaying it records redraws, not the file.

terminalProfiles.name: SSH
terminalProfiles.reason: Brings its own TTY, so a PTY recorder captures the remote session; local suspension is lost.

terminalProfiles.name: pwncat-cs
terminalProfiles.reason: Brings its own TTY, so a PTY recorder captures it.

terminalProfiles.name: Claude Code
terminalProfiles.reason: A full-screen TUI; the conversation comes from the local transcript when AI conversation capture is on.

terminalProfiles.name: Codex
terminalProfiles.reason: A full-screen TUI; the conversation comes from the local transcript when AI conversation capture is on.
